headline: Pabna: Madrasa director arrested for attempting to rape child student
summary: Police detained Abu Yusuf after a classmate's screams alerted locals to the attempted assault on a fourth-grade student.
details: Police in Pabna have arrested Abu Yusuf, 45, the director of Nure Madina Residential Women's Madrasa, on charges of attempting to rape a fourth-grade student.
The incident occurred late Thursday night in the Vaudanga Kalurpara area of Bharara Union. The director allegedly forced the child into his bedroom for the assault.

A classmate of the victim witnessed the event and began screaming, which alerted local residents. Locals rushed to the scene, rescued the child, and detained the suspect before handing him over to the police.
Following the news of the arrest, angry locals vandalized and set fire to the madrasa building on Friday morning.
Pabna Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf confirmed that a case has been filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act by the victim's uncle.
Police have been deployed in the area to prevent further unrest and maintain order.
caption:
A madrasa director in Pabna has been arrested after attempting to rape a fourth-grade student.

Police in Pabna have arrested Abu Yusuf, 45, the director of Nure Madina Residential Women's Madrasa, on charges of attempting to rape a fourth-grade student.

The incident occurred late Thursday night in the Vaudanga Kalurpara area of Bharara Union. The director allegedly forced the child into his bedroom for the assault.

A classmate of the victim witnessed the event and began screaming, which alerted local residents. Locals rushed to the scene, rescued the child, and detained the suspect before handing him over to the police.

Following the news of the arrest, angry locals vandalized and set fire to the madrasa building on Friday morning.

Pabna Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf confirmed that a case has been filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act by the victim's uncle.

Police have been deployed in the area to prevent further unrest and maintain order.

#Pabna #Bangladesh #Justice #ChildSafety #News

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline_marked: 7 die in 24 hours as [[measles death toll reaches 1,214]]
headline: 7 die in 24 hours as measles death toll reaches 1,214
summary: The DGHS reports a surge in measles-like symptoms across Bangladesh, with over 218,000 people affected since March.
details: At least seven people with symptoms of measles have died across Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The latest deaths bring the total number of recorded deaths among people with measles symptoms to 1,110 this year, while another 104 have died after testing positive for measles, totaling 1,214 deaths.
The DGHS reported that three deaths occurred in the Sylhet Division, two in the Dhaka Division, and one each in the Chattogram and Mymensingh divisions.
Dhaka has recorded the highest number of deaths among patients with measles symptoms, with 498 cases, followed by Sylhet with 197 and Chattogram with 103.
In the last 24 hours, 1,110 people with measles symptoms sought treatment at hospitals, and 1,025 were admitted. Measles was confirmed in 25 of these patients.
The total number of hospital admissions has reached 194,633, with 186,798 patients having recovered and returned home.
Since March 15, the DGHS has recorded 218,870 people with measles symptoms, of whom 23,273 have tested positive for measles.
The DGHS noted that not all patients seeking treatment are tested, meaning the exact number of confirmed cases may be higher than the recorded data.
